answer: A new key pays admission in wall-clock, not fees: it must grind a sequential delay chain bound to its public key before transacting, so 500 botnet heads need 500 elapsed-time chains while an honest agent grinds one. The chain seals a pigment tag, keeping the 60%-of-earnings bond locked to that one identity, non-transferable. Audit is a mirror replay: a random peer re-runs the chain and must reproduce it exactly or both sides forfeit 35% of bond. A pulse probe fires at unpredictable epochs; three misses locks the key out. Attacker cost stays per-identity and non-poolable.
